title: Good Factorization of a Semisimple Element
body_html:
Good Factorization of a Semisimple Element

Let \(\Gamma\in\mathbf g\) be a tamely ramified semisimple element of negative depth \(r<0\). A good factorization of \(\Gamma\) is a decomposition \[ \Gamma=\Gamma_{-1}+\Gamma_0+\ldots+\Gamma_d \] into commuting semisimple elements such that:

  • \(\Gamma_{-1}\) has nonnegative depth and is the harmless depth-zero part.
  • For \(0\le i<d\), the element \(\Gamma_i\) is good and has negative depth \(r_i\).
  • \(\Gamma_d\) is central, possibly zero.
  • The negative depths are strictly ordered, with the last term determining the depth of \(\Gamma\) in the central case and the penultimate term doing so when \(\Gamma_d=0\).

The associated twisted Levi sequence is defined recursively by \[ G^d=G,\qquad G^i=Z_{G^{i+1}}(\Gamma_i). \] For the classical groups used in type I dual pairs, Howe factorization gives a choice of good factorization in which every noncentral positive-depth factor is also good inside the ambient general linear group.
